entry.title: Transfer customer sales order price to adv. intercompany PO and sales order – Scope items 5D2 / 7DM
entry.content:
Hello everyone,

We are implementing Advanced Intercompany Sales in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition using the following scope items:

  • 5D2 – Advanced Intercompany Sales

  • 7DM – Advanced Intercompany Sales – Make-to-Order and Variant Configuration

We need guidance on how to achieve consistent pricing across the original customer sales order, the intercompany purchase order, and the intercompany sales order.

The original customer sales order is created through an external webshop interface. The interface provides condition PPR0 and additional surcharge conditions. Together, these conditions determine the sales order item’s price.

The system subsequently creates the intercompany purchase order in the selling company and the intercompany sales order in the delivering company.

Currently, the price from the original customer sales order is not adopted in the intercompany purchase order. Instead, the purchase order receives a significantly lower price, which appears to be derived from material-related master data or inforecord. The price discrepancy therefore already occurs when the intercompany purchase order is created.

Our requirement is to use the same price per item throughout this document chain. The selling company should pay the delivering company the same price that it charges the external customer, so that no trading margin remains in the selling company from this resale.

For illustration, if the original sales order contains a base price of EUR 1,000 and surcharges of EUR 250 per unit, both the intercompany purchase order and the intercompany sales order should have a price of EUR 1,250 per unit.

Does anyone have an idea or approach on how we can implement this in the public cloud?

Thank you!

Krys

SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

entry.title: Guidance Required on BAdI for Updating Supplier Invoice Item-Level Custom Fields via A2A API
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

In SAP S/4 HANA Public Cloud, we have a requirement to read the reference Purchase Order (PO) details while creating a supplier invoice from a third-party system and use those details to update item-level custom fields in the Manage Supplier Invoices application.

Initially, we identified the BAdI LOG_EDI_MM_INVOICE_CE_MAP. However, this BAdI is intended for B2B integration, whereas our third-party system uses the A2A service. Therefore, the BAdI is not triggered when creating a supplier invoice through the API.

We also explored an alternative approach by manually posting or parking supplier invoices in SAP and attempting to update the custom field values using the following BAdIs:

  • MRM_MRIS_DATA_MODIFY_CE

  • MRM_MRDC_DATA_MODIFY_CE

  • MRM_ERS_DATA_MODIFY_CE

However, none of these BAdIs is triggered during the supplier invoice posting or parking process.

Could you please suggest the appropriate BAdI or enhancement option to retrieve the reference PO details from the supplier invoice and update the item-level custom fields in Manage Supplier Invoices, particularly when invoices are created through the A2A API?

Any relevant SAP documentation, knowledge base articles, or technical blogs addressing this scenario would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks in advance for your support.

Best regards,

entry.title: Purchase Order Accruals calculation
entry.content:
Dear All,

We onboard a consultant on a six-month contract with a daily rate of GBP 100. As per the contract agreement, the maximum billable days are limited to 22 days per month.

We do not use the Service Entry Sheet (SES) concept in SAP. Therefore, we need to manage the Purchase Order (PO) and monthly accrual postings without service entry confirmations.

We are facing the following challenges:

Scenario 1: Maintaining the PO quantity as 6 months

If we maintain the PO order quantity as six months, the system calculates the PO value based on 180 days × GBP 100, resulting in GBP 18,000. This is incorrect because the contractual maximum is 22 billable days per month.

The system also calculates accruals based on the actual calendar days in each month (30 or 31 days), resulting in incorrect accrual amounts.

Scenario 2: Maintaining the PO quantity as 132 days

If we maintain the PO order quantity as 132 days (22 days × 6 months), the PO value is correctly calculated as GBP 13,200.

However, the accrual calculation is still incorrect. For example, for October 2026, SAP calculates an accrual of GBP 3,100 (31 calendar days × GBP 100) instead of the expected GBP 2,200 (22 billable days × GBP 100).

Clarification Required

How can we achieve the correct PO valuation and monthly accrual calculations using standard SAP functionality, considering that we do not use Service Entry Sheets?

Our requirements are:

Maintain the PO value at GBP 13,200 for the six-month contract.
Calculate monthly accruals based on 22 billable days, resulting in GBP 2,200 per month.
Prevent the system from calculating accruals based on calendar days.
Use standard SAP PO and accrual functionality without custom development, wherever possible.
Please advise on the recommended standard SAP configuration and process to ensure that both the PO value and monthly accrual postings are aligned with the contractual terms, without using the Service Entry Sheet process.

 

Thanks

Naveen
